edition.notes: A copyrighted twentieth-century English selection and translation, not the complete Triads: the volume prints seven thematic sections (A-G) drawn from the nine treatises, with Meyendorff's introduction and notes. It is registered because it is the only English witness this repository has reached for Palamas's own words; it is not public domain, and consumers may quote only short clauses with attribution and must not incorporate bulk text. Section and treatise numbers printed in this edition (for example III.i.29, III.ii.5) are the loci to cite. No exact artifact is registered: the copy read was an optical-character transcription of a scanned printing, which is a discovery and reading aid and not a collated witness, and consumers record that ceiling locally. The underlying fourteenth-century Greek is public domain and is a separate, unregistered edition; nothing here identifies it.
edition.publication: Gregory Palamas: The Triads, ed. John Meyendorff, trans. Nicholas Gendle, pref. Jaroslav Pelikan, Classics of Western Spirituality (New York: Paulist Press, 1983)
edition.title: Gregory Palamas: The Triads — Meyendorff and Gendle selection

alternate_titles: In Defence of Those Who Devoutly Practise a Life of Stillness
work.author: Gregory Palamas
work.description: Gregory Palamas's nine treatises in three sets of three, composed between about 1338 and 1341 in defence of the hesychast monks of Athos against Barlaam of Calabria. The third Triad develops the distinction between the imparticipable superessential essence of God and the uncreated deifying energies in which creatures really participate, and denies that God is seen in his superessential essence either now or in the age to come. A locus is Triad.treatise.section, as III.i.29 or III.ii.8-10.
work.title: Triads in Defence of the Holy Hesychasts
